116 CLAUDE.md
# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.

What still applies:

- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
  play rather than from a new content hook.
- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.

lines: // Past the vertex plane, and still beside the vertex rather than somewhere
// else on the map that happens to lie on the far side of it.
+  const passed = along >= 0 && distance <= arrive + CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT + 1;
+  // AT A TURN THE BODY MUST ACTUALLY PASS THE VERTEX.
+  // Turning even a fraction of a unit early cuts the corner, and a cut corner
+  // swings the body's own projection AROUND the corner farther than the body
+  // walked in that frame. `routeProgressUnits` refuses that frame outright —
+  // its allowance is exactly the displacement it was given — and the refusal is
+  // permanent, because every later projection is then further beyond the
+  // allowance than the last. Measured with a walking body, four cut corners
+  // froze the eighteen-unit comparison at four. A straight vertex has no corner
+  // to cut, so arriving inside the stop radius is enough there.

input.content:
# Integration — movie repair progress (CG-IMPL-004 / CG-IMPL-005)

Run: `2026-09-05-after-the-hearth` · contract scene-v2 `4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`
Owner of this pass: integration engineer, source only. Root owns inbox, lock, gates, readiness, final evidence.

## Status: patch phase COMPLETE, all in-pass checks green

Two source files changed, both inside `production-lock.json#/allowedPaths`:

| path | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.ts` | `4f8abeb7cc3a…` | `deea059b75dd…` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts` | `289fde04e77d…` | `8e11edd1137e…` |

The other 94 files in `implementation-source-manifest.json` are byte-identical to the
signed snapshot; that was verified before the first edit and again after the last.
No contract, geometry, route, cue-set, copy, guidance-meaning or player-rule change.
No predicate, threshold, distance, occupancy or completion condition was relaxed.

## What was actually wrong, and what it now does

### CG-IMPL-004 — cadence deadlock (was: real hardware stall)

`applyCommonGroundRail` spent the screening dwell with `ctx.noteScreeningAction()`
and only then called `ctx.performStoryInteraction`, whose own first test is
`screeningActionReady()`. Every ch13 act was refused by the dwell the rail had
just paid for; the ready `[F]` prompt stood at the core for the whole 300-second
home movie.

The chapter rail no longer carries the cadence at all. `CommonGroundRailContext`
does not declare `screeningActionReady` or `noteScreeningAction`, so consuming it
from here is now a type error rather than a convention. The rail walks and calls
the shared performer, which re-resolves the live interaction at the body's real
position, refuses anything that is not the plan's id, and spends the dwell only
when an act actually happened. The stale `<= CG_CORE_REACH` gate went with it —
the resolver already carries the true reach for each rung.

### CG-IMPL-005 — stateless waypoint scan

`nextWaypoint` re-scanned the whole polyline every frame for the first point more
than 1.2 units from the body, so the walked start became the next target again the
moment the body left it. Replaced by an ordered controller cursor
(`runtime.railTraversal`) keyed on run, actor, world, beat, route and survey tail
revision. It advances only onto vertices the body has genuinely reached, never
reconsiders one behind it, and rebuilds from the body's own projection — never
from anywhere ahead of it — on a beat change, Continue, revision, route change or
any frame where the body is not on the leg the cursor believed it was walking.

It is controller state and nothing else: no predicate, guidance fact, marker or
receipt reads it. Every walked unit still comes from `routeProgressUnits` reading
actual frame-by-frame displacement, and every trace sample is still only where the
body actually stood.

## The three precision failures the multi-tick test exposed

The regressions drive a body that *walks* — bounded step per frame, stops inside
the requested radius — against the production predicates. Three real failures
appeared that a teleporting stub would have hidden:

1. **Corner cutting froze the comparison at 4 of 18 units.** Turning 0.18 units
   early swings the body's own projection *around* the corner farther than it
   walked that frame; `routeProgressUnits` refuses that frame, and the refusal is
   permanent because every later projection is further beyond the allowance. Raw
   frame-by-frame evidence retained in the report. Fixed by requiring the body to
   actually pass a turning vertex, and by aiming a short step through corners and
   through the far end so arc gain never exceeds displacement. Straight vertices
   keep the ordinary stop-radius arrival.
2. **The survey recording began up to two units short of S.** The first sample is
   written at the body's actual pose, and the approach line in from his inspection
   pose lands in the survey housing's shadow — S sits about 0.2–0.35 units from
   both that shadow and the 12-unit range edge. The offered span then failed his
   first-try test on an occlusion the authored route does not contain, and the
   movie fell back to the contingent witness. The rail now aims a step *through*
   the head along the route's own first leg and records only on arrival. Measured
   first sample is now 0.32 from S and the accepted class is `fixed-reference`,
   as signed.
3. **Blanket 1.2-unit stops undershot measured poses.** Every walk requested the
   same radius, against a 1.25-unit occupancy cylinder and a resolver reach wider
   than the intended arrival. Plans now carry their own `arriveRadius` (route
   0.35, pose 0.6, body 2.4, core 1.2 unchanged), and the far-reference and
   span offers wait for arrival instead of spending cadence on attempts the
   transaction will refuse.

Also corrected while here: `CommonGroundRailContext.walkToward`'s third parameter
was declared as a slow radius; the shared walker has no such parameter and was
receiving `0.8` as a gaze lift.

## New finding raised and fixed in-pass

`ch13-return` walked to `CG_POSES.W` at the pose radius. W is *his* mounted
inspection pose, not an empty mark, and the beat only needs 3.4 units. Stopping on
top of him would manufacture exactly the body-clearance stand-off this chapter
never resolves by displacing anybody. Now stops at body distance. No browser
evidence exists for this beat; it is a source-level boundary correction of the
same class, reported rather than assumed harmless.

`ch13-return`'s board / launch / fly / land grammar was checked line by line

## What was actually wrong, and what it now does

### CG-IMPL-004 — cadence deadlock (was: real hardware stall)

`applyCommonGroundRail` spent the screening dwell with `ctx.noteScreeningAction()`
and only then called `ctx.performStoryInteraction`, whose own first test is
`screeningActionReady()`. Every ch13 act was refused by the dwell the rail had
just paid for; the ready `[F]` prompt stood at the core for the whole 300-second
home movie.

The chapter rail no longer carries the cadence at all. `CommonGroundRailContext`
does not declare `screeningActionReady` or `noteScreeningAction`, so consuming it
from here is now a type error rather than a convention. The rail walks and calls
the shared performer, which re-resolves the live interaction at the body's real
position, refuses anything that is not the plan's id, and spends the dwell only
when an act actually happened. The stale `<= CG_CORE_REACH` gate went with it —
the resolver already carries the true reach for each rung.

### CG-IMPL-005 — stateless waypoint scan

`nextWaypoint` re-scanned the whole polyline every frame for the first point more
than 1.2 units from the body, so the walked start became the next target again the
moment the body left it. Replaced by an ordered controller cursor
(`runtime.railTraversal`) keyed on run, actor, world, beat, route and survey tail
revision. It advances only onto vertices the body has genuinely reached, never
reconsiders one behind it, and rebuilds from the body's own projection — never
from anywhere ahead of it — on a beat change, Continue, revision, route change or
any frame where the body is not on the leg the cursor believed it was walking.

It is controller state and nothing else: no predicate, guidance fact, marker or
receipt reads it. Every walked unit still comes from `routeProgressUnits` reading
actual frame-by-frame displacement, and every trace sample is still only where the
body actually stood.

the requested radius — against the production predicates. Three real failures
appeared that a teleporting stub would have hidden:

   walked that frame; `routeProgressUnits` refuses that frame, and the refusal is
   permanent because every later projection is further beyond the allowance. Raw
   frame-by-frame evidence retained in the report. Fixed by requiring the body to
   actually pass a turning vertex, and by aiming a short step through corners and
   through the far end so arc gain never exceeds displacement. Straight vertices
   keep the ordinary stop-radius arrival.

   written at the body's actual pose, and the approach line in from his inspection

# Integration movie repair — CG-IMPL-004 / CG-IMPL-005

Run `2026-09-05-after-the-hearth` · contract scene-v2
`4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e` · all three
signatures unchanged and binding · no contract, creative or player-rule change ·
no publication · no browser or GPU run · **no rendered or movie success is
claimed by this pass**.

Machine-readable companion: `integration-movie-repair-report.json`.

## Source boundary

Starting source verified byte-exact against `implementation-source-manifest.json`
(96 of 96) *before the first edit*. Two files changed, both listed in
`production-lock.json#/allowedPaths`; the other 94 signed files are still
byte-identical.

| path | before | after |

| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts` | `289fde04e77d2cba…` | `8e11edd1137ecffc…` |

Unified diff: `movie-repair.diff` (`814f5b54093ce1f6…`), per-file copies under
`evidence/integration-movie-repair/`.

## CG-IMPL-004 — the cadence the rail did not own

`applyCommonGroundRail` called `ctx.noteScreeningAction()` and *then*
`ctx.performStoryInteraction`. The shared performer's first test is
`screeningActionReady()`, so it refused every act against the dwell the rail had
just spent. That is the 300-second home movie sitting under a ready `[F]`.

The chapter rail no longer has the cadence to spend.
`CommonGroundRailContext` does not declare `screeningActionReady` or
`noteScreeningAction`; consuming it from here is now a compile error rather than
a convention someone has to remember. The rail walks and asks:

```ts
ctx.walkToward(goal, plan.arriveRadius);
ctx.performStoryInteraction(plan.interactionId as never);
```

The performer re-resolves what the player is actually being offered at this body
position, refuses anything that is not this plan's id, runs every transaction
predicate, and spends the dwell only when an act happened. The old
`<= CG_CORE_REACH` gate is gone with it — it applied the habitat core's 4.2-unit
reach to survey and common rungs the resolver measures at 2.0 and 3.4, and the
resolver already carries the true reach for each.

No milestone is granted, no resolver bypassed, no timeout rescue added.

## CG-IMPL-005 — ordered traversal

`nextWaypoint` rescanned the whole polyline every frame for the first point more
than 1.2 units from the body, so the walked start was retargeted the moment the
body left it. It is replaced by an ordered cursor in `runtime.railTraversal`,
keyed on run, actor, world, beat, route identity and survey tail revision.

- advances only onto vertices the body has genuinely reached;
- never reconsiders a vertex behind it during ordinary forward walking;
- rebuilds from the body's **own projection** — never from anywhere ahead of it —
  on a beat change, Continue, revision, route change, or any frame where the body
  is not on the leg the cursor believed it was walking;
- is read by no predicate, guidance fact, marker or receipt.

Walked units still come only from `routeProgressUnits` reading actual
displacement; trace samples are still only where the body actually stood;
occupancy, footing, reference, clearance and completion predicates are untouched.

## What the walking test found that a teleporting stub would not

The regressions drive a body that walks — bounded step per frame, stops inside
the requested radius, asserted never to exceed one frame's travel — against the
production predicates. Three real failures surfaced.

**1. Corner cutting froze the comparison at 4 of 18 units.** Turning 0.18 units
early swings the body's projection *around* the corner farther than it walked
that frame. `routeProgressUnits` caps a frame's gain at that frame's
displacement, so it refuses the frame — and the refusal is permanent, because
every later projection is further beyond the allowance than the last. The
reference and footing checks were true the whole time; nothing else was failing.
Raw frame log retained at `evidence/integration-movie-repair/corner-seam-raw-failure.txt`.

Fixed by making the body actually walk the corner: a turning vertex is consumed
only once the body has passed it, and goals aim a short step through corners and
through the polyline's far end so arc gain never exceeds displacement. Straight
vertices keep ordinary stop-radius arrival. After the fix the same diagnostic run
advances continuously and the production predicate closes on its own at frame 91
— about four seconds of walking for eighteen units. **The predicate was not
touched. The body was made to walk.**

**2. The survey recording began up to two units short of S.** The first sample is
written at the body's actual pose, and the approach line in from his inspection
pose lands in the survey housing's shadow — S sits roughly 0.2–0.35 units from
both that shadow and the 12-unit range edge. The recorded opening samples were
occluded, his first-try test stopped on an occlusion the authored route does not
contain, and the movie fell back to the contingent witness — losing the
fixed-reference class the long route was chosen to demonstrate.

The approach now aims a step through the head along the route's own first leg,
and the rail records only on arrival; the act reach is the aim plus the stop
radius, so the body can never settle outside the reach it is waiting on. Measured
after: first sample 0.32 from S, every sample clean from the fixed reference,
accepted class `fixed-reference`, no witness. The player-facing resolver reach is
unchanged — only what the rail does with it.

**3. One blanket 1.2-unit stop for every move.** Plans now carry their own
`arriveRadius` — route 0.35, pose 0.6, body 2.4, habitat core 1.2 unchanged — and
the far-reference and span offers wait for arrival instead of spending cadence on
attempts the transaction will refuse.

Also corrected: `CommonGroundRailContext.walkToward` declared a third parameter
the shared walker does not have (a slow radius); the rail was passing `0.8` into
the gaze lift.

## Standing clear of his body

After offering the span the body stands on its own last recorded sample, which is
on the span he then has to walk. The rail now steps off the trace with ordinary
movement, under the same clearance rule that holds his leg — and explicitly not
by offering a witness, which repairs an end he cannot reach and has never
repaired a body standing in the way. The genuine witness branch for real
reference holds is preserved, as is the common beat's existing stand-clear during
his positioning leg. Proven end to end: he walks her span himself and the beat
reaches `tested` with no witness and no hold outstanding.

## New findings

**CG-IMPL-006 (medium, fixed in pass, `ch13-return`).** The on-foot approach
walked to `CG_POSES.W` at the pose radius. W is his *mounted inspection pose*,
not an empty mark, and the beat advances at 3.4 units — stopping on his body
manufactures the body-clearance stand-off this chapter never resolves by
displacing anybody, and the tightened pose radius would have made it worse. Now
stops at body distance. There is no browser measurement of `ch13-return`; this is
a source-level correction of the same class, reported rather than assumed
harmless.

**CG-IMPL-007 (info, no defect).** `ch13-return`'s board / launch / fly / land
grammar was checked line by line against the shipped ch10 and ch12 idioms in
`autopilot/primitives.ts`. They match, and `requestLanding` is guarded and
edge-safe. No change made.

worldgen.

verified before the first edit and again after the last.

- `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts` `289fde04e77d…` → `8e11edd1137e…`

shared performer, whose first test is `screeningActionReady` — so every act was
refused against the dwell the rail had just paid for, which is the 300-second
home movie under a ready `[F]`. The rail no longer carries the cadence at all:
`CommonGroundRailContext` does not declare it, so consuming it is a type error.
The performer owns resolution, proximity, transaction predicates and the dwell.

**CG-IMPL-005.** The stateless polyline rescan is replaced by an ordered
controller cursor with honest reconstruction across beat, Continue, revision and
route identity. It is read by no predicate; walked units still come only from
`routeProgressUnits` over actual displacement.

**Movement precision.** A multi-tick regression that *walks* a body against the
production predicates found three real failures a teleporting stub would have
hidden: corner cutting permanently froze the comparison at 4 of 18 units; the
survey recording began up to two units short of S, inside the housing's shadow,
costing the fixed-reference class; and one blanket 1.2-unit stop served route
waypoints, a 1.25-unit occupancy cylinder and body approaches alike. All three
were repaired by making ordinary movement precise enough for the existing
proofs. **No predicate, threshold, distance, occupancy or completion condition
was relaxed, and no milestone is granted by any rail.**

**New findings.** CG-IMPL-006 (`ch13-return` approached W at the pose radius,
onto W-7744's own mounted inspection pose — fixed in pass, no browser evidence
for that beat exists). CG-IMPL-007 (`ch13-return` flight grammar matches the
shipped ch10/ch12 idioms — no defect, no change).

none removed or weakened) · build 0 · scene AV, chapter registry, chapter
journey, story ladder, guidance targets, story authority, catalog and creative
workflow gates all 0 · triad implementation gate 0, 1708 checks. Both defects
were temporarily reinstated to prove the new regressions bite (6 and 4 failures
respectively); source restored and re-hashed after each.

run on a GPU, played or listened to in this pass. The real headed ch13 home,
survey and common movie belongs to the independent verifier. The limitations
listed above otherwise stand unchanged; CG-IMPL-001, CG-IMPL-002 and CG-IMPL-003
remain open.

`iterations/implemented-scene-v2/` (`68f5b276…`, the hash
`implementation-gate-pass.json` cites); the post-repair run is kept at

(20 entries, listed under `hashRefresh`) so this canonical report matches the
final combined implementation.
EOF

Done. Both defects are fixed, proven, and reported.

## What was wrong

**CG-IMPL-004** — `applyCommonGroundRail` spent the screening dwell via `ctx.noteScreeningAction()` and *then* called `ctx.performStoryInteraction`, whose first test is `screeningActionReady()`. Every ch13 act was refused against the dwell the rail had just paid for. That is the 300-second home movie under a ready `[F]`.

The chapter rail no longer *has* the cadence to spend — `CommonGroundRailContext` doesn't declare it, so consuming it is now a compile error, not a convention. The shared performer owns resolution, proximity, transaction predicates and the dwell. The stale `<= CG_CORE_REACH` act gate went with it (it applied the core's 4.2 reach to rungs the resolver measures at 2.0 and 3.4).

**CG-IMPL-005** — the stateless polyline rescan is replaced by an ordered cursor keyed on run/actor/world/beat/route/tail-revision, with honest reconstruction from the body's own projection, never from ahead of it. No predicate reads it.

## What the walking test found that a teleporting stub would have hidden

I wrote the regression to walk a body against the production predicates, and it failed three times for real reasons:

1. **Corner cutting froze the comparison at 4 of 18 units.** Turning 0.18 units early swings the body's projection *around* the corner farther than it walked that frame; `routeProgressUnits` refuses that frame and the refusal is permanent. Fixed by walking through turning vertices, not across them. The predicate was not touched — the body was made to walk. Raw frame log retained as the producer asked.
2. **The survey recording began up to two units short of S**, in the housing's shadow, which cost the `fixed-reference` first-try class the long route was chosen to demonstrate. Now aims through the head and records on arrival; measured first sample 0.32 from S, class restored.
3. **One blanket 1.2-unit stop** served route waypoints, a 1.25-unit occupancy cylinder and body approaches alike.

## New findings

**CG-IMPL-006** — `ch13-return` walked onto W-7744's own mounted inspection pose; my tighter pose radius would have made it worse. Now stops at body distance. No browser evidence exists for that beat, so I reported it rather than assuming it harmless. **CG-IMPL-007** — its flight grammar matches the shipped ch10/ch12 idioms; no defect, no change.

## State

Two files changed, both in `allowedPaths`; the other 94 signed files verified byte-identical before the first edit and after the last. Typecheck 0, 348 files / 3026 tests (baseline 3018, +8), build 0, all static gates 0, triad gate 1708 checks. Both defects were temporarily reinstated to prove the regressions bite (6 and 4 failures); source restored and re-hashed.

Two things to flag: the triad gate **rewrites** the run-local `creative-run-quality-report.json` as a side effect — I restored it to root's archived hash and kept my post-repair run in evidence, so re-issue it if you want it to reflect this source. And nothing here was rendered, run in a browser or on a GPU; no movie success is claimed. The real headed ch13 movie remains the verifier's.
